body:
## Problem
Recent changes (#40249) caused neovim to change the terminal cursor to blinking on exit.

## Solution
Save the current terminal cursor style on startup and restore it on exit instead of always using "\x1b[0 q".

This uses DECRQSS[^1] to query the terminal, reads the number from the DECRPSS[^2] reply, and saves it into a new `char[6]` variable in the `tui` struct.

Fixes: Blink after exit #40560
Fixes: unsetting 'guicursor' does not disable cursor shape change #38987

## Rationale
Neovim is treating DECSCUSR 0 (printf "\x1b[0 q") as 'reset cursor to default'. This is not how it worked historically.

The DEC manual [^3] (section 5-127 (page 281) and section 4-23 (page 161)), as well as vt100/vt510 [^4] (and other historical sources) say 0 and 1 are both the same, blinking:
```
  Ps	Cursor Style
  0, 1 or none	Blink Block (Default)
  2	Steady Block
  3	Blink Underline
  4	Steady Underline
```
 Ghostty documents it as such, and foot [^5] admits:
> “In ctrlseq, **\e[0 q** (or \e[ q for short) is described **to have the exact same semantics as \e[1 q**, but foot instead treats 0 to mean "reset to the configuration defaults".”

Tested and working in xterm, foot, and ghostty.

References:
[^1]: https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/DECRQSS.html
[^2]: https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/DECRPSS.html
[^3]: https://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/dec/terminal/vt5xx/EK-VT520-RM_VT520_VT525_Programmer_Information_Jul94.pdf
[^4]: https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/DECSCUSR.html
[^5]: https://codeberg.org/dnkl/foot/issues/218

comment_regular_data.body:
I am not sure if `tui->saved_cursor_style` is the best place to save it, or if it will affect anything else to add fields to this struct. I am open to any changes.
I know that it interferes with the tests, test/functional/terminal/tui_spec.lua returns the DECRPSS answer in the  'actual' output which is not in the 'expected'.

I am not sure how to write a test for this 'external' behaviour'.

I admit I do not understand how the `terminfo_set_str()` function constructs or applies its values. I would, possibly, prefer to save just the number and then merge it back into the string when it is run.

Any input is welcome.

in principle this sounds good, idk if there's a reason we weren't doing this. cc @kylesower @gpanders 


but this PR as-is needs work. e.g. usually a response is asynchronous and is received in `tui/input.c`

> Any input is welcome.

i don't have time to spend on this, if others don't chime in, and you can't figure it out, then we'll have to close this.

> but this PR as-is needs work. e.g. usually a response is asynchronous and is received in `tui/input.c`

Thanks. I was confused about how to get that response, I will take a look at input.c.

I was also not sure if I needed to uncook the terminal `~(ICANON|ECHO)` or if that was already done. I ran out of time before I thought to check. :)
these days, this may be possible to do 100% in Lua, see `runtime/lua/vim/tty.lua` for other examples where we query and get responses.

> these days, this may be possible to do 100% in Lua, see `runtime/lua/vim/tty.lua` for other examples where we query and get responses.

Even when the c code explicitly sends "\x1b[0 q" at a late stage?
Doing this resulted in the old trick of `VimLeave` sending the desired code not working since tui.c was sending a 'set blinking' after that.

My lua skills are worse than my c skills. :)

> Neovim is treating DECSCUSR 0 (printf "\x1b[0 q") as 'reset cursor to default'. 

Neovim is using the escape sequence for the "reset cursor style" terminfo entry to reset the cursor style. Not all terminals define this sequence (it is an extension), and not all define it correctly, so we do our best where we can.

> This is not how it worked historically.
>   ```
> 0, 1 or none	Blink Block (Default)
> ```

I see the word default right there :D. But we don't use this exact sequence for all terminals. Only ones where we more or less know what it should be. If a terminal doesn't have a concept of a "default" cursor style, users have many options:
- use a better terminal
- use a shell that sets the style to what they want (like fish)
- override definitions with `$NVIM_TERMDEFS` (not yet included in release version)

I considered using DECRQSS for https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40800; however, [not all terminals support DECRQSS](https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/issues/7184), and [we](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/40988) [have](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/40526) [seen](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/39337) [several](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/39661) [issues](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/28776) from sending unrecognized escape sequences.

Given there's already so much custom logic related to all these different terminals, it felt like we may as well just bake it in.

> > ```
> > 0, 1 or none	Blink Block (Default)
> > ```
> 
> I see the word default right there :D.

But we don't want to set it to set some default, we want to set it to what the user had configured prior to running neovim.

>  But we don't use this exact sequence for all terminals. Only ones where we more or less know what it should be.

But that list also includes ones where we _know_ that is _not_ "what it should be". 0 only works on foot and ghostty, from what I can tell, it explicitly sets block blinking on xterm and urxvt and others that follow the vt100 and DEC 'standard'.

> If a terminal doesn't have a concept of a "default" cursor style, users have many options:
>  ...

Or to ask the terminal what it was set to and put it back to that.

> Given there's already so much custom logic related to all these different terminals, it felt like we may as well just bake it in.

Yes, but it is being baked in in a way that breaks xterm (and others that follow what DECSCUSR said (from DEC and it is the DEC CURSoR option:)).

> not all terminals support DECRQSS

That is a problem. We should find a way to check if they do and only use this on ones that behave.

> I considered using DECRQSS for #40800; however, [not all terminals support DECRQSS](https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/issues/7184), ...

I tested with alacritty, and, while DECRQSS does not return an answer, it does no harm.

However, my code hangs waiting for the read. But, now that I have a terminal to test this with, that can be resolved.

> But we don't want to set it to set some default

Why not? The docs are somewhat ambiguous because they say, "To disable cursor-styling, reset the option...."

xterm doesn't agree with its own documentation because it defaults to a steady block even though it calls blinking block the default on [this page](https://www.invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html). We can't really take any of these "standards" as absolute truth. However, xterm does define `Se` as `\E[2 q` (which many terminals incorrectly define), and since the default out of the box is steady block, we may wish to use that for xterm.

> 0 only works on foot and ghostty

It works on [most modern terminals](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/38987#issuecomment-4274073845). We might need another look at which terminals we set it for. https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40249 was a bit of an experiment in response to https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40234#issuecomment-4702249873. 

> I tested with alacritty, and, while DECRQSS does not return an answer, it does no harm.

Did you test with the 100 other terminals that people use? DECRQSS caused some of those issues I linked, which is why it can now be disabled in multiple ways.

~~Rather than all this logic of querying different things that different terminals may or may not support, we could also have an option to set the cursor to a specific style on exit for those people who have an issue. Not sure I like that, though.~~ I don't like this idea because it can be handled by `$NVIM_TERMDEFS`.

> > But we don't want to set it to set some default
> 
> Why not?

Because they are using 'default' differently, it seems. They do not mean "what the user chose/wants" they mean ... I don't know what they mean...
> The docs are somewhat ambiguous because they say, "To disable cursor-styling, reset the option...."

I have not seen that phrasing, but, yeah...

> xterm doesn't agree with its own documentation because it defaults to a steady block even though it calls blinking block the default

Yeah, I know, that is a pain, and `\e[0 q` and `\e[1 q` are the same thing, making it redundant. I did submit a patch to xterm, but there is reluctance to change the historic behaviour. :)

>  However, xterm does define `Se` as `\E[2 q` (which many terminals incorrectly define), and since the default out of the box is steady block, we may wish to use that for xterm.

Yes, that seems like a solution, it tells us what to use. However that is statically defined, right? So it does not take into account what the user has set in their config or command line?

I would much rather use what they say to use than using what we use now, since that means neovim definitely changes the xterm cursor on exit.

> Did you test with the 100 other terminals that people use?

No, I only use xterm. Which worked fine up to a month and a bit ago.

> Rather than all this logic of querying different things that different terminals may or may not support, we could also have an option to set the cursor to a specific style on exit for those people who have an issue. Not sure I like that, though.

Why don't you like having an option? We used to have the in the form or manually setting it in the `vimLeave` `au`, but that does not seem to work anymore.
It would be better if the option were scriptable, so the user can check their terminal or environment and set it for relevant machines.

> > The docs are somewhat ambiguous because they say, "To disable cursor-styling, reset the option...."
> 
> I have not seen that phrasing, but, yeah...

Sorry, that comes from `:h guicursor`. It can also be reworded to whatever we want it to mean (e.g. "To use terminal default cursor, ...")

> > xterm doesn't agree with its own documentation because it defaults to a steady block even though it calls blinking block the default
> 
> Yeah, I know, that is a pain, and `\e[0 q` and `\e[1 q` are the same thing, making it redundant. I did submit a patch to xterm, but there is reluctance to change the historic behaviour. :)

I figured such a thing would be problematic. I assume making `\E[0 q` set the default configured cursor would be similarly problematic.

> > However, xterm does define `Se` as `\E[2 q` (which many terminals incorrectly define), and since the default out of the box is steady block, we may wish to use that for xterm.
> 
> Yes, that seems like a solution, it tells us what to use. However that is statically defined, right? So it does not take into account what the user has set in their config or command line?

Yes, it doesn't take into account the `~/.Xresources` config for xterm. xterm uses the configured cursor only on startup, and doesn't use it for the `\E[0 q` sequence. I'd be surprised if there are many applications which restore it properly when it's configured as something other than steady block.

> I would much rather use what they say to use than using what we use now, since that means neovim definitely changes the xterm cursor on exit.

Yeah, that much was a regression.

> > Rather than all this logic of querying different things that different terminals may or may not support, we could also have an option to set the cursor to a specific style on exit for those people who have an issue. Not sure I like that, though.
> 
> Why don't you like having an option? We used to have the in the form or manually setting it in the `vimLeave` `au`, but that does not seem to work anymore. It would be better if the option were scriptable, so the user can check their terminal or environment and set it for relevant machines.

Because we already have a way to configure it, and I think it'll be confusing to add another one specifically for this one terminal feature. I'm not sure when the `VimLeave` method broke, but that should be probably be fixed since people were already relying on it. I suppose we must send the reset cursor style sequence after `VimLeave` now.

> I assume making `\E[0 q` set the default configured cursor would be similarly problematic.

Asking xterm to change 40 year old behavior (that people might rely on) is hard, but we are talking about adding an option (possibly `\e[7 q` ) to query the configuration (all the needed data is accessible) and set the cursor to what it was. Presumably `Se` would then point to that and if neovim uses what `Se` says it will work as expected.

> Yes, it doesn't take into account the `~/.Xresources` config for xterm.

Hopefully that will come in xterm 411 with the new option 7.

> ... I suppose we must send the reset cursor style sequence after `VimLeave` now.

I can test tomorrow when I am back at a machine.

> > I assume making `\E[0 q` set the default configured cursor would be similarly problematic.
> 
> Asking xterm to change 40 year old behavior (that people might rely on) is hard, but we are talking about adding an option (possibly `\e[7 q` ) to query the configuration (all the needed data is accessible) and set the cursor to what it was. Presumably `Se` would then point to that and if neovim uses what `Se` says it will work as expected.

That would be good. I think that's a better approach than DECRQSS given that DECRQSS will introduce more problems where we have to treat different terminals in a special way (and potentially introduce ~~more blocking waits into nvim startup~~, more config to disable it, etc.). This will benefit applications other than nvim as well.

I imagine most applications don't really need to "restore cursor to what it was before," but just want "set it to the user's preference."

In the meantime, I can put up a PR to restore the old behavior for xterm.

> In the meantime, I can put up a PR to restore the old behavior for xterm.

Great, thank you.

> I'm not sure when the VimLeave method broke, but that should be probably be fixed since people were already relying on it.

Never mind, I agree with @gpanders here: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/36863#issuecomment-3627224271

> > I'm not sure when the VimLeave method broke, but that should be probably be fixed since people were already relying on it.
> 
> Never mind, I agree with @gpanders here: [#36863 (comment)](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/36863#issuecomment-3627224271)

Can't say _I_ do.

> One application (nvim) should not be responsible for setting the cursor shape in another application (your shell). If you want your cursor to be a beam in your shell then the "right" place to do that is in your shell.

This conflates the _shell_ and the _terminal_. If "one application should not be responsible for setting the cursor shape in another" then the shell should not be the one to set the shape in the terminal. The shell has no access to this information, and can't even query what is should use since neovim already changed it from what the user set.

Using the shell is a bit of a blunt instrument, but so is using an autocmd. But the shell PROMPT-COMMAND is a blunt instrument that hits on _every_ program invocation, whereas the VimLeave au only hits after vim has changed the cursor and made it necessary.

> Some terminals (e.g. foot) interpret the "reset cursor shape" (Se) control sequence to set the cursor shape back to whatever is defined at the terminal level. Other terminals interpret that sequence as just resetting back to a block cursor.

Agreed. Neovim should 'reset the cursor' since neovim changed it, but it should use the terminal feature (`Se`) to do so. If terminals don't do this correctly the terminal needs to be fixed...

But, allowing the user to choose to run a command as vim/neovim exits is orthogonal to resetting the cursor —that is but one application of the `au`— this should be done as late as possible so their choice is not overwritten by choices hardcoded into neovim.

One wonders if there should not also be a `VimLeavePost` that triggers as late as possible, but users assume that `VimLeave` already does this. `VimLeave` can reset the cursor in vim, it is just neovim that does its own reset after `VimLeave`.

The question seems to be about the position of those two functions, surely the neovim reset should (and could) happen before the `VimLeave` event.

> > One application (nvim) should not be responsible for setting the cursor shape in another application (your shell). If you want your cursor to be a beam in your shell then the "right" place to do that is in your shell.
> 
> This conflates the _shell_ and the _terminal_. 

No. He was talking about setting the cursor in the shell. e.g. in fish `set fish_cursor_default block`. This way you don't have a million programs that run under the shell that have to program the same logic to remember or reset the cursor. You just have the shell set it to the desired value after every command. The shell should work defensively if you don't want users to constantly hit issues like this. In fact, my shell cursor is different from my terminal, but I've never run into this problem because my shell sets the cursor at every prompt.

> But the shell PROMPT-COMMAND is a blunt instrument that hits on _every_ program invocation

Why does this matter?

> Agreed. Neovim should 'reset the cursor' since neovim changed it, but it should use the terminal feature (`Se`) to do so. If terminals don't do this correctly the terminal needs to be fixed...

We do.

> But, allowing the user to choose to run a command as vim/neovim exits is orthogonal to resetting the cursor —that is but one application of the `au`— this should be done as late as possible so their choice is not overwritten by choices hardcoded into neovim.

Are there other use cases blocked by the exact timing?

> Are there other use cases blocked by the exact timing?

Not that I am aware of, just the one under question. I never used the feature till I tried to deal with this issue. :)
But the ability for the user to change the cursor when leaving vim still has benefit, they might not be exiting into a shell (mc (midnight commander), yazi, nnn, lf, for instance are all 'terminal file mangers' that often run vim as their editor) and the cursor change can affect them too. This is probably not a high priority, since the terminal should facilitate resetting that, but, if it is not onerous to reorder when these bits run (it worked before) it would be nice.
